title: Survive the Research Timeout
objective: Keep the research brief alive when a slow source hangs.
description: Two sources feed this research brief: a fast status blog and a creaky old archive. A Timeout block already stops the archive from hanging forever - but stopping is all it does. One slow response and the whole brief dies. Put a Retry block in front of the Timeout so the archive gets a few tries before you give up on it. The archive is slow on its first two attempts and answers on the third.

sample_input.topic: Acme API rate limits after the March outage

expected_output: A brief with a headline, at least two key points, and both research sources listed.

config.prompt: Write a research brief from the two sources. Return JSON with headline, key_points and sources.
config.system: You are a research analyst. Cite every source you used.

solution_hint: Drop a Retry block between 'Fetch the status blog' and 'Give up after 4s', and set max attempts to 3. Guards stack: the Retry decides how many tries the archive gets, the Timeout decides how long each try may take.

failure_scenarios.label: The archive hangs
failure_scenarios.description: The research archive does not respond on the first two attempts. The third attempt comes back normally.

detail.message: The research archive did not respond in time.

completion_criteria: A Retry block protects the archive fetch
The archive fetch recovers instead of ending the run
The published brief lists its sources
The run finishes at the Output block

data.headline: Acme tightened API rate limits after the March outage
key_points: Acme cut the burst allowance from 240 to 120 requests per minute on 14 March.
The archive shows the same limits were briefly trialled in 2024 and rolled back.
Customers on the legacy plan keep the old limits until renewal.

acme-status-blog.title: Rate limit changes following the March incident
acme-status-blog.content: On 14 March we reduced the burst allowance from 240 to 120 requests per minute for all new plans. Legacy plans keep their previous limits until renewal.

research-archive.title: Acme rate limit history, 2023 to 2026
research-archive.content: Acme trialled a 120 request per minute burst allowance in 2024 and rolled it back after two weeks. The March 2026 change reinstated it permanently.
